Theme

Body, health & movement

pulse noun

heartbeat

also feel someone’s pulse, take someone’s pulse, heartbeat

classical

Quint. 7.10.10: sentīre pulsūs vēnārum (Lewis & Short s.v. pulsus)
Tac. A. 6.50: pulsum vēnārum attingere (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 65: vēnārum pulsus, with vegetior, fast, and languidior, weak

pulsus vēnārum

the pulse

The pulse was felt in the veins.

Other words

  • vēnās tentāre — feel someone’s pulse

    classical · Quint. 11.3.88 (Lewis & Short s.v. tentō); Suet. Tib. 72 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 65: vēnās (pulsum vēnārum) alicujus tentāre

Examples

  • pulsus vegetior (languidior)

    a fast (weak) pulseTraupman 366

See also vein, heart, doctor.

SourcesLewis & Short: pulsus · Lewis & Short: vena · Lewis & Short: tento

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 65.
